key_insight: At finite squeezing, continuous-variable graph states obey topology constraints that rule out exact qumode local-addition analogues of qubit local complementation or qudit local addition.
engineering_relevance: The equivalence criterion can help determine whether experimentally accessible imaginary graph states can be converted into desired real graph states using Gaussian local unitaries.
method: Propagate graph-based conditions to construct a Gaussian local conversion or prove its impossibility.
Derive topology relations for equivalent real and purely imaginary graph states.
Use canonical forms to establish rigidity and define approximate local addition at sufficiently strong squeezing.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical equivalence criteria and impossibility results, with no experimental data or numerical benchmarks described.
watch_item: Approximate local addition requires sufficiently strong squeezing; the abstract provides no quantitative squeezing threshold or approximation-error bound.
paper_title: Graphical Rigidity of Continuous Variable Graph States under Gaussian Local Transformations
